entries.clue: Grow quickly, providing benefit everyone participates in (7)

indicators.note: everyone takes part inside the benefit, so ALL sits within BOON

annotation.surface: An investment scheme that swells fast because the rewards are shared by all who join.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a pitch for a profit-sharing scheme; 'everyone participates in' pictures the whole group sitting inside the benefit.
annotation.definitionFit: To balloon is to swell rapidly, as costs or a waistline can.

entries.clue: Criminal has sack full of diamonds for example (3,3)

indicators.note: the sack is filled with the other letters, so they go inside BAG

blocks.note: D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

annotation.surface: A burglar makes off with a swag bag stuffed with diamonds.
annotation.walkthrough: The swag bag of jewels is exactly what a thief would carry, which hides that 'diamonds' is just the suit letter D.
annotation.definitionFit: A bad egg is a rogue or wrongdoer, a loose informal fit for criminal.

entries.clue: Pressurise poor over working (4,2)

indicators.note: in a down answer, the first piece sits over the second

blocks.note: lean = meagre, poor, as in lean times
on = working, as a switched-on machine is

annotation.surface: A boss piles pressure on badly paid staff to work harder.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Over' only works because this is a down clue: LEAN is written above ON.
annotation.definitionFit: To lean on someone is to put pressure on them.

entries.clue: Unhappy when husband leaves having no underwear? (3,2,5)

indicators.note: the husband departs, so H is taken out

blocks.note: out of shorts = having no shorts, i.e. no underpants

annotation.surface: A comic picture of someone grumpy because they have run out of clean underwear.
annotation.walkthrough: In Britain shorts can mean boxer shorts, i.e. underpants; strip the H from OUT OF SHORTS and you are left feeling off-colour.
annotation.definitionFit: Out of sorts means slightly unwell or in a low mood.

entries.clue: Pulling up some off-grid anarchist – it’s a low point (5)

indicators.note: in a down clue, pulling up reads the letters from the bottom upwards
only part of the phrase is used

annotation.surface: An anarchist living off the grid has hit rock bottom.
annotation.walkthrough: The letters straddle the gap between the two words, and read upwards as the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Nadir is the astronomical term for the point directly beneath the observer, used figuratively for the lowest point of anything.

entries.clue: Gives up and prepares to travel home (5,2)

annotation.surface: Someone quits and gets ready to head back home.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Packs in' is a British phrase for quitting, as in packing in a job.
annotation.definitionFit: To pack something in is to stop doing it or give it up.

entries.clue: Decaying muon lit up some dangerous stuff (9)

indicators.note: decay breaks something down, so the letters fall apart and rearrange

annotation.surface: A physics lab note: a decaying particle glows and reveals something hazardous.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole surface is particle physics, and 'decaying' is both radioactive vocabulary and the instruction to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: Plutonium is a radioactive, highly toxic element.

entries.clue: Ocean life regularly features this young animal (4)

indicators.note: take every other letter, at regular intervals

annotation.surface: A nature documentary line: this baby creature often appears in sea life.
annotation.walkthrough: Whale calves really are ocean life, so the surface is true as well as the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A calf is the young of a cow, whale, elephant and others.

entries.clue: Skinny kid putting together some barbecue food (5,3)

blocks.note: to kid is to tease, or rib

annotation.surface: A thin child helps assemble food for a cookout.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Kid' looks like a noun for a child, but here it is the verb: to rib someone is to kid them.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: spare ribs are one of the classic things cooked on a barbecue.

entries.clue: It’s important component of gunboats (4,4)

blocks.note: the letters N and B sit side by side in gunboats, and NB is the familiar abbreviation used in notes

annotation.surface: A remark that some key part of a warship matters.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half is cryptic: the component is not a gun or engine but the letters NB inside 'gunboats', short for nota bene, Latin for 'note well'.
annotation.definitionFit: Nota bene is written to mark a point as important.

entries.clue: An early version of old copper vessel (5)

blocks.note: d = the old penny, a copper coin in pre-decimal British money
a raft is a simple vessel

annotation.surface: A museum label: a primitive form of an antique copper pot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Old copper vessel' looks like one antique pot; it splits into an old penny (d) and a boat. 'Copper' is not a policeman here either.
annotation.definitionFit: A draft is a first, rough version of a piece of writing.

entries.clue: Entertainers turn on match (6,3)

indicators.note: in an across answer, the turn goes on (after) the match

blocks.note: a double is an exact match
a performer's turn is their act

annotation.surface: Comedians switch on their act for a big sporting fixture.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Turn on' looks like a phrasal verb and 'match' like a game; both are nouns in the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A double act is a pair of entertainers who perform together.

entries.clue: Congratulations for being so healthy (4,3,3)

blocks.note: an exclamation of praise for someone's success
said of wholesome food or exercise that benefits the listener

annotation.surface: Someone is praised for keeping so fit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Good for you!' is praise, and healthy food is also good for you, so one phrase answers both halves.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Good for you!' is an exclamation of congratulation.

entries.clue: English auntie dismisses conservative retreat (3)

indicators.note: auntie sends the conservative away, so C is dropped

blocks.note: Auntie is a nickname for the BBC, Britain's public broadcaster

annotation.surface: A British aunt snubs a Tory relative at a family getaway.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital-less 'auntie' looks like a relative; it is Auntie, the BBC.
annotation.definitionFit: To ebb is to recede or fall back, as the tide does.

entries.clue: Society is not safe from this religious gatekeeper (5,5)

blocks.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe

annotation.surface: Nobody in society is safe from the one who judges at heaven's gate.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Safe' reads as an adjective, but it is the noun: a peter, the safe a safecracker blows.
annotation.definitionFit: Saint Peter is traditionally the keeper of the gates of heaven.

entries.clue: Against constant reversal in position – it delays waste elimination (12)

indicators.note: the constant's letters are turned round
the reversed constant goes inside the position

blocks.note: con = against, as in pros and cons
a station is a position or post

annotation.surface: Opposing a constant flip-flop of stance, which holds up getting rid of rubbish.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like politics or recycling; the definition is the bodily kind of waste elimination.
annotation.definitionFit: Constipation is difficulty in emptying the bowels, delaying the elimination of waste.

entries.clue: Shocking for a bird when taking temperature (9)

indicators.note: the bird takes in the temperature, holding T inside

blocks.note: the starling is a common bird

annotation.surface: It is a shock for a bird to have its temperature taken.
annotation.walkthrough: 'When' is filler joining the bird to its action; the T slides in after STAR.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something that startles gives you a jolt, just as a shock does.

entries.clue: Cabin on health resort sounds daring (8)

indicators.note: the answer is said like the words before it

blocks.note: cabin = HUT, then health resort = SPA; said together they give the sound

annotation.surface: Staying in a hut at a spa is described as a bold move.
annotation.walkthrough: Chutzpah comes from Yiddish; its CH is pronounced as a throaty H, which is why HUT-SPA sounds right.
annotation.definitionFit: Chutzpah is audacity, a nerve or daring bordering on cheek.

entries.clue: Runs around animal shelter – magic (4,4)

indicators.note: the runs wrap around the shelter

annotation.surface: Someone races round an animal shelter as if by magic.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Animal shelter' suggests a rescue centre, but the biblical ark is the one meant.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: the dark arts are sorcery and black magic, a phrase popularised by Harry Potter.

entries.clue: Encouraging core faction to hold on to weapon (12)

indicators.note: the faction holds the weapon inside it

blocks.note: the heart is the core of something
a wing of a party is a faction

annotation.surface: An inner group of a movement keeping its weapons is an inspiring sign.
annotation.walkthrough: The core-faction-weapon sequence sounds like a militia briefing, far from the warm feeling of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: news that warms the heart lifts the spirits, as encouraging news does.

entries.clue: Weak charge almost drained (6)

indicators.note: not quite the whole word, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: bled = drained, as of blood; drop the D

annotation.surface: A battery with only a weak charge left is nearly drained.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Charge' reads as electric, and 'drained' as a battery; they are a fee and bled.
annotation.definitionFit: Feeble means weak or lacking strength.

entries.clue: Setter follows one out to get gold or silver perhaps (6)

indicators.note: one (I) is put out of the word

blocks.note: the setter refers to themself as me
to tail someone is to follow them

annotation.surface: A puzzle-setter trails a rival to win a medal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Follows' looks like the order of pieces, but it is the word TAILS itself.
annotation.definitionFit: Gold and silver are examples of metals; 'perhaps' marks them as examples.

entries.clue: Express disapproval when adult has left chore (3)

indicators.note: the adult departs, so A is removed

blocks.note: A = adult, a film certificate; removed

annotation.surface: A grumble when the grown-up walks off and leaves the housework undone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tsk' is the tutting sound of disapproval, spelt without a vowel.
annotation.definitionFit: Tsk is a click of the tongue expressing disapproval.

entries.clue: Ape mother’s complicated mood (10)

indicators.note: the letters are tangled and rearranged

annotation.surface: A mother gorilla is in a complicated frame of mind.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ape' looks like a verb for mimicking, and the apostrophe S is part of the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Atmosphere is the mood or feel of a place or occasion.

entries.clue: Character immersed in some game (5)

indicators.note: the answer is sunk inside the following words

annotation.surface: A player gets totally absorbed in a game.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Character' looks like a person in a role-playing game; it is a letter of the Greek alphabet.
annotation.definitionFit: Omega is a character, the last letter of the Greek alphabet.

entries.clue: Opening of false accounts conceals troubling truth (4)

indicators.note: take the opening letter of each word that follows

annotation.surface: Fraudulent bookkeeping hides an uncomfortable truth.
annotation.walkthrough: The grammar is off-key ('accounts conceals') because the four initials had to be the right words.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a fact is what is actually the case, the truth.

entries.clue: Arranging vague trip to find cure for 14? (9)

indicators.note: the letters are put in a new order

annotation.surface: Planning a loose sort of journey in search of a remedy for a blocked gut.
annotation.walkthrough: The cross-reference is to 14 across, CONSTIPATION; the question mark flags the jokey pairing.
annotation.definitionFit: A purgative is a laxative, which relieves constipation.

entries.clue: Return information found in a small piece of bone (5)

indicators.note: the finished string is sent back, read right to left
the information letter sits inside the small piece

blocks.note: I = information, as on tourist signs

annotation.surface: Sending back data discovered in a fragment of bone, as an archaeologist might.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is an archaeology report, which hides that 'a small piece' is the letters A BIT.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the tibia is the shin bone, the larger of the two in the lower leg.

entries.clue: Add label to minced food – it’s a pound sign (7)

indicators.note: one piece is added to the other, the label going after the food

blocks.note: hash is a dish of chopped meat

annotation.surface: Sticking a price label on some mince, marked with a pound sign.
annotation.walkthrough: In the US the # symbol is called the pound sign; British readers think £, which is the misdirection.
annotation.definitionFit: A hashtag is written with #, which Americans call the pound sign.

entries.clue: Close to having 22 missing (7)

annotation.surface: Being near to lacking an atmosphere.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Close' is the adjective for stuffy weather, not 'near'.
annotation.definitionFit: Close weather or a close room is airless and stuffy.
